---
title: "Short session – the housing-audit case"
subtitle: "Two halves of about seventy-five minutes, with a facilitator"
---
The [case study](../../cases/housing/index.qmd), which presents the original study, the Multi100 project, the five reanalyses and the SCORE replication on which every format of the case is built, is the place to start.

This is the short session on the housing-audit case, for a slot of two to three hours, and it runs entirely in the [browser lab](../../cases/housing/lab.qmd), a page of the course site on which R runs inside your browser: nothing is installed, nothing is sent to a class chart and nothing is preregistered. The session works on a field experiment, in which emails that differed only in the name that signed them were sent to public housing authorities in the United States, and on a claim of the original authors (OAs) that five analysts reanalysed for Multi100. You meet the claim and the five analysts, write the estimand statement behind the claim, and reproduce one of the five reanalyses, whichever you choose. Then you try a few alternative analyses from the menu of the case, read the place of the one that you would defend among the 64 specifications on the curve of the claim, and end on the replication that tested the claim with new data.

The session runs as two halves of about seventy-five minutes, with a break of fifteen minutes between them. The class writes its estimand statements and its reproduced values in the chat and sends them at the same moment, so the session needs a facilitator. The one-day courses on [methods](../housing-one-day-methods/index.qmd), [open science](../housing-one-day-open-science/index.qmd) and [data tools](../housing-one-day-data-tools/index.qmd) take the same case through a whole day, each with its own focus.

| | What happens | Length |
|---|---|---|
| [Before the session](before.qmd) | Read the case study and open the browser lab once. | about an hour |
| [First half – The claim and its reproduction](half-1.qmd) | The three Rs and the SCORE programme, the paper and the five analysts, the estimand statement and the causal graph; then you reproduce one of the five reanalyses. | about 75 minutes |
| [Second half – Exploration and replication](half-2.qmd) | The specification menu, a few analyses of your own and the place of one of them on the curve of 64, and the replication with new data. | about 75 minutes |
| [After the session](after.qmd) | The rest of the exercise, and where to go next. | as you like |
